lines.dialogue: Thanks. PASSENGER #2 Hi, precious.
for her) Hi. We just adopted her. From Vietnam. We're bringing her home for the first time. PASSENGER #3 She's such a little angel. I can just tell you're going to be a daddy's girl, aren't you?
Let's hope so. END OF ACT ONE
Okay...
Oh, please, you like pie.
Not as much as y-- Oh my God, you have blueberry on your fingers.
This doesn't worry you, that she barely slept on the plane and she's still wide awake? I didn't even think Asian eyes opened that wide.
Maybe she just can't fall asleep unless she feels a woman's shape. That orphanage was all women.
I just thought--
Now you're sensitive about that? It wasn't a problem on Halloween when you just had to be Sarah Palin and I was stuck all night in that John McCain harness.
I have not been --

Yeah, it's funny isn't it? Hilarious! This baby would have grown up in a crowded orphanage if it weren't for us "twinkies" and I'd think someone like you would have a little sympathy for people who are a little different than --
What?!
What the hell is it?
Yeah, I see. With wings.

Like fairies, you mean. Okay, now I get it. "Yes, we pulled you out of your home in Vietnam, but don't worry, things will be perfectly normal here. Your dads are floating fairies." You know, I really don't need my family ridiculing me over this tonight. Call Andre and have him paint something... less gay.
A triptych of us having sex would be less gay.
Nothing.
I never told them, all right?
I never told my family we were adopting a baby.
We weren't telling anyone until we knew it was official and then when the agency called last week I had to, you know, pack and --
Okay fine, my family was going to have a big opinion and I just didn't want to hear it.

I've got good reason to be nervous. I'm having flashbacks to when I told my family I was gay. My mom cried for a week and my Dad still does this thing where he announces himself before walking into any room we're in to make sure he doesn't see anything.
Uggghhhh. I don't know if I can do this.
Hey guys!
Oh, thanks.
Don't worry, Dad, nothing gay going on in here. May I take your multi- colored coat and jeweled cap?
Oh, it was great. But about that, I actually have something I need to tell you guys...
We didn't just go there for pleasure... We kind of have some big news.
So anyway... about a year ago, Cam and I started feeling this longing for something... more.
Anyway --
We adopted a baby.
That's why we went to Vietnam. Her name is Lily.
I know. I can't believe it either.
So... what do you think, grandpa?
Her, Dad. I'll change her.
I don't know. Maybe I thought you'd try to talk me out of it.
I haven't told her yet, but that was a good sneak preview.
Not much. I just know her mother was sixteen.
Thanks. I just hope...
I already love her so much and... it's hard enough for any kid, let alone one with two dads. What if, when she gets older, she's ashamed of us?
All right.
What? FADE TO BLACK.
Cam, hurry up. We’re going to be late.
Let’s not make this an episode of “The Cam Show”. CAMERON People love “The Cam Show”. MITCHELL Yes, I know. CAMERON It’s appointment viewing.
I’m Mitchell, this is Cameron, and this is Lily.
Hello, I’m Mitchell and I’m a lawyer. And this is Cam.
Cam...

Oh good, now we can open that general store. I thought we were just here for diapers. CAMERON We had an old saying back on the farm: as long as you’re bringing the mule to market -- I feel you rolling your eyes, Mitchell. CAMERON It was at one of Pepper’s game nights that we met... I remember Mitchell because he kept rolling his eyes every time I got a little boisterous -- MITCHELL I was not. CAMERON You were a little.

Let’s just get the diapers and get out of here. CAMERON Fine, I just want to swing by the wine section. MITCHELL There’s a wine section? CAMERON A good one. Just past the tires. MITCHELL No way, they don’t have -- Oh my god. The paper shredder I wanted. Confetti and crosscut.
Cam, what is this place?
You got it.
You’re not going to believe what I saw -- coffins. They have baby formula and they have coffins. You can buy everything you need from birth to death.
Oh my god, look at all these diapers. These are so cheap, why don’t we just buy enough for the next year or two?
They sell sheds here.
Yeah, really nice. Not that he’s ever said anything like that to my boyfriend...
No, it’s not okay.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: Please don’t spike our baby. And why is she dressed like the Hamburglar? CAMERON She’s a referee. MITCHELL Do we even have to go to my dad’s? CAMERON Are you kidding? We’re playing Notre Dame.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: Yeah, she’s ready.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: I’m just a little worried about C.J. Hightower. With that bad ankle I don’t know how he’s gonna run his corner routes. CAMERON What did my boyfriend just say? MITCHELL Well, I heard what you said and I thought I should make an effort to learn about football. CAMERON That’s very mature of you. MITCHELL I figured, how hard can it be if football fans can learn it? CAMERON (O.S.) That’s very elitist of you. MITCHELL I’m sorry, it’s just... sometimes I feel a little superior to people who

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: I didn’t know he knew that term.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: And I’ve got to tell you I’m a little worried about C.J. Hightower. With that bad ankle I don’t know how he’s gonna run his corner routes.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: So who then will be running the corner routes?

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: Billings. Could you imagine? CAMERON Play action. JAY Nah, they’re running it. CAMERON Trust me -- look, look, play action. He’s open, he’s open, he’s got it. Touchdown! JAY Lucky. MITCHELL Maybe they should have just considered blitzing. JAY What? Not with those linebackers. Get out of here. CAMERON Admit it, we’re giving you a better game than you thought. Don’t mess

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: Well, there’s kind of a lot of drama.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: You’re asking us if you’re attractive?

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: You look great, Dad. CAMERON Very distinguished. JAY Distinguished? That’s like calling a woman handsome. I’m trying to find out if Gloria is walking around with the troll under the bridge. MITCHELL You’re not a troll. JAY So if I was sitting in one of your bars and there’s some Righteous Brothers playing, would you, I don’t know, check me out? MITCHELL Get out of here. JAY Yeah, fine. Whatever. MITCHELL
Everything we own is pointy. Why is our daughter dressed like Donna Summer?
I thought you were done with this.
Who’s talking?
I just think this might be a little over-the-top.
I’m loose. I’m fun. Remember last week? Breakfast for dinner. That was my idea.
Is she wearing eye shadow?
I can’t, I’m late for work.
It is a good song.
Okay... Big finish, and --
If it was her head, I think she’d be --
Yeah, it was her head.
Why do you have chocolate on your face?
So, you ate your way to it?
Do you think she’s okay?
Maybe that’s a bad sign. Let’s try to make her laugh.
That’s how we’ll know she’s fine. Where’s doggy?
Moo.
I know. That’s why it’s funny. Moo.
Yeah right, so she can be all judgmental and condescending -- like she’s the expert and we don’t know how to take care of a baby.
Hey, not a big deal -- just wondering. When your kids were small did you ever, I don’t know... smack their heads into a wall?
No, accidentally. We just kind of bonked Lily’s head. It wasn’t really that hard, and she isn’t acting different, but --
Thanks for your help.
We’ve got to take her to the doctor.
It happened a couple hours ago. On a door jamb. DR. MIURA Ouch. DR. MIURA (CONT’D) There doesn’t seem to be any mark.
Yes, like a hat.
Really? You thought “ghetto fabulous” might be medically relevant. DR. MIURA Maybe I should just finish the exam.

She hasn’t laughed since the head bump. I showed her a stuffed dog and said “Moo” and she just stared at me... kind of like you’re doing. Maybe it’s a cultural thing. DR. MIURA Just to be safe, show me how hard Lily got hit. Use your head.
Um... okay.
I guess it was something like this. DR. MIURA Can I see that again? DR. MIURA (CONT’D) How are you feeling?
Fine. DR. MIURA So is Lily. Babies are designed to survive new parents. Stop worrying. You guys are doing great.
Maybe you should do this.
I don’t want to bump her head against the door or pinch her with the seat belt.
It’s just... I think I suck at being a father.
Except that you’re like a natural at this. You walk in the room and she lights up. You can change a diaper with one hand. Nice, huh, I’m actually jealous of you.
It was just a few forms...
I still can’t believe you were going to wait until she was “old enough.”
We are.
We are.
Okay. I think we just locked our baby in the car.
Let’s not panic.
Help! We locked our baby in the car and people are judging us!
Don’t break the window you’ll get glass on her. OPERATOR (V.O.) Sir, please tell your wife to relax. Everything is going to be okay.
That’s a man. OPERATOR (V.O.) Really?
Check the doors.
Would this be easier for you if we suspended you from a crane?
You always take it too far.
Your nephew’s first birthday party --
You brought a wind machine --
A wind machine!
Sure, it’s his chance to be the father of a champion. Well, second chance. We all know how the first one went.
Nothing happened.
This is interesting to no one.
Eleven.
Figure skaters! Oh, for godsakes I’ll tell the story.
Yes, my sister and I were a team. A pretty good team. We were called “Fire and Nice.”
I was “Fire,” because of the red hair, and she was “Nice,” because it was ironic and she wasn’t.
It wasn’t some meet. It was the Central California thirteen and under championship. Just the Emerald City at the end of my yellow brick road. CAMERON Wow. You just made figure skating even gayer.
No!
Okay, maybe I was a little resentful. But that’s embarrassing and petty and not a good color on me. It’s like you and yellow.
It kind of makes you look like the sun.
I knew you didn’t have a meeting!
No.

Okay, I guess I am still a little angry. You stole my moment. CLAIRE Twenty-one years ago. MITCHELL It didn’t matter to you because you had plenty of your own moments -- cheerleading, school plays, making out with the quarterback --
But we had to keep it a secret. You shouldn’t have quit, it was selfish. CLAIRE Okay, fine. You want to know why I quit? I did it to protect you.
From what? Glory?
Of course.
I’m sorry. I know it probably seems so petty.
Well sure, it’s harder now, you’ve let yourself go.
Look, I’m glad Dad’s proud of Manny. But... I don’t know... it would have been nice to see him that proud of us... of me.
I never claimed any of this was rational. I’m sorry for being such a pill.
I never really loved skating.
Okay, this is going to sound a little gay...

When you and I skated together, you weren’t the mean older sister and I wasn’t the clingy little brother. We were a team. And let’s face it, as teenagers, or when Mom and Dad got divorced, and even now, we’re always on opposing sides. I guess I... miss being on your team.
Where are you going?
What?
Oh my god, you’re not serious?
